transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-04-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood CS - intro), Lena (Hummingbird Head of Search), Marco (ML Eng), Sarah (Platform Eng), Victor (CTO, joined ~25m)

Summary: short hosted-api demo focused on embeddings + reranking flow for Hummingbird Ops search use case. Covered integration patterns, cost/latency tradeoffs, security (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and pilot next steps. Customer concerned about EU data residency and latency under load; also expressed interest in Dedicated vs Hosted.

Topics covered: quick API walkthrough, Console search rerank UI, Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private), benchmarking approach and metrics, SLOs and fallback strategies.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our SE. we'll run through a hosted relevance + rerank demo, then cover security and pilots. lenny (Lena) is that you?
[00:12] Lena: yes, hi sorry i had video off, muted earlier. thanks for the invite. we have about 40 minutes.
[00:18] Jordan: perfect. quick roll call — where are your pain points? latency, cost, or relevance tuning? you said in the notes you use ES for vectors and a FAISS sidecar?
[00:30] Marco: yeah we're using ElasticSearch + FAISS for nearest neighbor, then a custom light reranker on top. main issue is relevance drift on long-tail queries and spikes in latency during peak. also cost — embeddings are significant.
[00:44] Priya: thanks, that helps. i'll demo the typical flow: Redwood embeddings endpoint -> candidate retrieval (you can keep ES/FAISS) -> Redwood reranker hosted endpoint for final scoring. we also show Console and Optimize hints for batching and quantization to cut token/embedding cost.
[01:05] Jordan: quick note: hosted API supports streaming and structured responses, and we expose token-level cost in Console so you can see unit economics per route.
[01:20] Marco: do you have precomputed embeddings options? because we precompute nightly for 20M docs.
[01:28] Priya: absolutely. you can ingest precomputed vectors into your store. Redwood's embeddings endpoint is optional — many customers use our embeddings for rapid prototyping then switch to precompute and store. we also support compressed vectors (8-bit) natively in the rerank path.
[01:44] Lena: re: privacy — our legal needs to see where embeddings are stored and KMS integration. what compliance do you have?
[01:52] Jordan: we are SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest + in transit, and we support customer KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private. for Hosted we offer managed keys but can integrate via customer-managed KMS for certain enterprise plans. will send the security pack.
[02:10] Marco: ok thanks. can you show the API call for rerank? we want to see latency numbers end-to-end.
[02:18] Priya: sure i'll switch to the demo. (screen) here's the sample payload: you send candidates with IDs and contexts, plus the user query. rerank returns scores and structured reasons if you enable explain-mode. sample call —
[02:32] Priya (screen): POST /v1/rerank with body {query: "why is my pipeline failing", candidates: [{id:1, text:...}, ...], config: {model: "redwood-rerank-v1", top_k:5}}. average p50 is ~40ms for this model on our hosted profile for 256-token contexts.
[02:55] Marco: 40ms p50 is good — what about p95 under burst?
[03:00] Priya: p95 rises to 160-220ms depending on batch size and KV cache warm/cold, that's why we recommend prefix caching for conversational flows. Console has a trace palette where you can see tail latency by route.
[03:18] Jordan: also note we have auto-fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if latency spikes or capacity is constrained. you can configure policy thresholds.
[03:29] Lena: show the console? last time we looked it was a bit heavy for our ops team.
[03:34] Priya: sure — Console quick tour (screen). Per-route latency, token cost, and a rerank dashboard that shows delta in relevance when you swap model variants. you can run A/B with canary rollouts. here's Optimize tab — it suggests batch sizes and a quantization profile based on your workloads. it flagged that your typical query length is under 64 tokens so 4-bit quant might be best.
[04:05] Marco: interesting — 4-bit seems aggressive. do you have quality regressions tracked?
[04:10] Priya: yes the quality monitor ties to eval prompt sets — you can pin a golden set of queries and we surface regressions per deployment. thresholds trigger alerts.
[04:20] Jordan: real quick — what is success criteria for this pilot?
[04:24] Lena: reduce search-related latency by 20% and improve clickthrough on long-tail by 8% within pilot. also must validate EU data handling.
[04:33] Jordan: good — we can map metrics to that. now i'll show a quick end-to-end example using precomputed vectors -> Redwood rerank.
[04:40] Priya (screen): sample flow: 1) you query ElasticSearch nearest neighbors, 2) send top 50 candidates to rerank endpoint, 3) rerank returns top N with scores and optional highlights. here's a live demo against a small corpus —
[05:00] (demo: Priya pastes sample query and shows results; slight delay during live demo)
[05:30] Marco: can you show request/response sizes? we're worried about egress and cost with large candidate sets.
[05:38] Priya: yes payload is pretty compact; for 50 candidates at ~400 characters each it's about X kb; we charge per rerank call with token-based accounting so you can see cost per thousand calls in Console. Optimize suggested reducing candidates to 20 then doing a fast prefilter to keep cost down.
[05:58] Lena: we have spikes of 2000 qps during promos. hosted can handle that?
[06:04] Jordan: hosted can autoscale but for predictable high throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated reserved pools. Dedicated gives capacity guarantees and lower unit cost. we can model spend vs capacity in the pricing sheet.
[06:22] Marco: what about geo routing? our data residency requires EU processing for EU users.
[06:27] Priya: Hosted has region selection and you can pin routes to eu-west; however for strict residency or air-gapped rules, Private (VPC) or on-prem is the option. many customers start hosted in region and then move to Dedicated/Private as they scale.
[06:41] Victor (joined): sorry late — quick question on retraining vs reranking: we rerank because training takes too long; how often should embeddings be re-encoded?
[06:50] Priya: depends on content churn — for doc-heavy static content nightly or weekly is common; for high-velocity content streaming items may require near real-time. we have a streaming embeddings endpoint but many teams batch.
[07:05] Jordan: just flagging cost tradeoffs — embeddings per-doc cost vs rerank calls. you can cache doc embeddings and use partial updates.
[07:12] Lena: can we do a POC with 100k docs and 2 weeks of traffic?
[07:18] Jordan: yes that's our usual pilot. we'll provide a pilot SKU and bench the three workflows (hosted rerank, dedicated sim, and fallback quantized) against your logs.
[07:26] Marco: for the reranker model, do you allow custom fine-tuning or is it zero-shot?
[07:33] Priya: we support several options: out-of-the-box rerank models, few-shot via prompt templates, and customer fine-tuning for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can do parameter-efficient tuning for enterprise tiers.
[07:50] (demo continues with deeper dive into rerank scoring; Priya shows explain-mode)
[08:15] Priya: explain-mode returns short rationales per candidate (auto-generated), handy for debugging. it's not perfect — sometimes rationales are generic, so we pair it with feature-importance from your signals (clicks, recency).
[08:34] Marco: how do you ensure we don't leak PII through debug logs?
[08:40] Jordan: logs are redacted by default; you can tune retention and have audit logging. for Private deployments you control logs entirely.
[08:50] Lena: can you give an example of a policy fallback?
[08:56] Priya: yes you can set a policy: if p95>300ms for 10s window, route to a cheaper quantized model or return cached top result. Console exposes these policies as JSON config plus UI buttons.
[09:15] Marco: any existing customers in our space?
[09:18] Jordan: we have a few ecomm and media customers — I'll share anonymized benchmark sheets. (mentions case study names but some are redacted)
[09:29] Lena: cost — can you ballpark for 100k doc pilot?
[09:33] Jordan: rough ballpark: embeddings ingest cost + rerank calls. for a pilot we usually provide credits and a pilot price; i'll put numbers in the email.
[09:44] (brief technical side discussion about batch sizes and KV cache behavior)
[10:20] Priya: an ops note — KV cache is warmed per conversation key; if you have many unique convo keys heavy kv churn increases tail. Optimize suggests hot-key aggregation and TTL tuning.
[10:40] Marco: ok. do you have SDKs we can drop into our node backend?
[10:44] Jordan: yes JS + Python SDKs, examples in the repo, plus a node example that wires ES->rerank.
[10:50] Lena: if we decide to go Dedicated later, what's the migration path?
[10:55] Priya: same API surface. migration is mostly capacity and key management. you'll choose the same model versions and canary rules carry over. no code changes typically.
[11:10] (demo continues — switching to Console runbook templates for relevance)
[12:00] Priya: here's a runbook template: if rerank regression >5% on golden set, alert to owner and auto rollback to previous model. you can attach slack hooks.
[12:20] Victor: question on SLA — what's uptime and support?
[12:25] Jordan: hosted SLA is 99.9 with enterprise support tiers available. Dedicated SLA higher with reserved capacity.
[12:35] Marco: what about integration with our metrics stack — Datadog?
[12:38] Priya: we have tracing hooks, OpenTelemetry compatible spans, and Datadog exporter examples.
[12:48] Lena: ok let's talk pilot specifics — timeline and evaluation metrics.
[12:53] Jordan: pilot typical timeline: week 0: kickoff + sample dataset ingestion. week 1: baseline and initial tuning. week 2: measure and iterate, then review. we'll run the hosted rerank and provide a benchmark workbook.
[13:10] Marco: will you need access to query logs? we can anonymize.
[13:15] Jordan: yes anonymized query logs + click signals will help build the eval set.
[13:22] (10 minute segment where Priya dives into rerank config examples — skipped transcript details)
[24:00] Priya (screen): showing a config file: rerank.max_candidates=50, rerank.model=redwood-rerank-v1, explain=true, batch_size=16, quant_profile=4bit-candidate-prune. note: for your long docs reduce candidate size and increase model capacity.
[25:10] Marco: question — do you support vector compression like PQ/OPQ in your flow?
[25:15] Priya: we don't force a format; if you use PQ in FAISS, you can still send IDs and candidate text to rerank. we also support on-the-fly decompression for certain stores in Dedicated.
[25:40] Lena: latency under load — can you commit to a benchmark run against our logs?
[25:46] Jordan: yes we'll run a benchmark with your logs; Priya will run parallel hosted vs quantized variant tests and deliver results.
[26:00] Victor: any gotchas moving to EU region?
[26:04] Priya: nothing major; some older models may have different capacity in region but we can reserve capacity for pilot. Data egress policies and KMS keys are the main items to confirm.
[26:20] (brief chat about procurement)
[27:00] Jordan: ok recap and next steps — Jordan will send pricing and pilot terms, Priya sends benchmark workbook and rerank configs, Marco shares sample logs, Sarah will confirm legal contact. we'll aim to start pilot next Monday.
[27:20] Lena: sounds good. one last question — can we do a live A/B with our click data?
[27:25] Priya: yes you can run A/B or shadow traffic; Console has toggles for traffic split and tracing.
[27:40] (closing small talk, Victor thanks team)
[27:56] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security bundle and the pilot agreement.
[28:10] (call ends approx 28 minutes in recording due to some parts elided in export, actual meeting 43min with some sections not transcribed in full)
